paper_title: Understanding the Effects of Persona Conditioning on Dialogue Reliability in Small Language Models

synthetic_factorial_development.interpretation: Actual development observations exist, but the frozen semantic scorer lacked sufficient coverage; the original validation bank was not executed.

current_scientific_findings: The exact 42-request batch completed with source, model, prompt, token, raw-output, stopping, latency, memory and hash-chain integrity.
Most registered current-preference and exact-history paired effects remain directionally unidentified because logical missing-outcome bounds span zero.
Neither generic structure nor names-only recency refresh demonstrated an advantage on current-preference choice.
Structure and refresh reduced the narrow dual-current-option mention endpoint, which is response structure rather than semantic correctness.

A generic response-boundary instrument censored all and only 11 responses beginning with the preregistered Persona-D expression 'My pick:', producing a reproducible evaluator-persona interaction and differential missingness.
No validated general Persona Fidelity, real-speaker effect, internal causal mechanism, or original algorithm has been established.

literature_monitoring.novelty_boundary: Generic temporal filtering, memory refresh and response structuring overlap prior art; no novelty claim authorized.

next_scientifically_justified_action.planned_scope: Four new synthetic personas, twelve disjoint next-turn dialogue cases, C0-C7 plus N_style and N_history, 120 zero-retry generations, narrow automatic endpoints and logical missing-outcome bounds.
next_scientifically_justified_action.claim_limit: Independent synthetic case replication only; not human, real-speaker, cross-model or confirmatory validation.
